title: U.S. transmission needs, load-growth expectations, and comparison rules
interpretation: These studies answer different questions. They are juxtaposed for dashboard comparison but are not spliced into one synthetic forecast.

retained_results.context: central decarbonization futures with accelerated transmission frameworks

study_comparison.geography: United States regions and interregional interfaces
study_comparison.method: review and synthesis of published planning studies

retained_results.context: announced or expected retirements cited in the assessment

study_comparison.major_driver: large commercial and industrial loads, especially data centers

study_comparison.geography: Eastern, Western, and ERCOT interregional interfaces
study_comparison.method: reliability stress cases and interface-specific transfer additions
study_comparison.retained_results: Use the interface-level tables and maps; do not publish a fabricated single national GW total.

load_shape_cross_reference.historical_scope: 53 demand-reporting balancing authorities, 13 EIA regions, 83 reported BA-subregions

coincident_reporting_footprint_2024.boundary: EIA-930 reporting footprint, not a perfectly bounded Lower-48 control total

analytical_join: Use UTC hour ending to compare coincident BA and regional demand.
Use each BA's local hour ending for customer-facing daily shape.
Join forecasts to the same geography, weather year, and accounting boundary before comparing peaks.
Compare peak MW, energy TWh, ramp MW per hour, and seasonal timing separately.
A national annual TWh forecast cannot be converted to a corridor requirement without spatial production-cost and power-flow modeling.
load_shape_cross_reference.forecast_gap: No public, unified BA/subregion hourly forecast through 2050-2070 was found. The dashboard must keep annual long-run projections separate from regional ten-year peak forecasts and historical hourly observations.

requirements: never interpolate sparse milestones without a visible line-style flag

dashboard_panels.reason: National public hourly interface shadow-price data are not uniform; ISO/RTO-specific acquisition is required.

requirements: tooltip includes source and study year
zero accreditation is visually distinct from missing

key_conclusions: Load growth and generation siting make more transmission valuable in every major study reviewed, but the amount is scenario-dependent.
The next transmission problem is not only annual energy delivery: noncoincident regional peaks, steep ramps, winterization, and a small number of high-congestion hours determine many network needs.
Interregional transfer improves resilience only when neighboring regions have available resources during the same stress event; transfer capability is not generation.
A corridor catalog can communicate scale, but a defensible needs comparison ultimately requires nodal or zonal production-cost and AC contingency analysis.
